Git Feature-Branch Push: `git push <remote> <branch>`, `git push <remote> <local-ref>:<remote-branch>`, `git push <remote> HEAD:<branch>`, and `git push -u <remote> <branch>` where the destination branch name is NOT `main`, `master`, `trunk`, `develop`, `production`, or matches `release/*` / `prod/*`. Creating a fresh feature branch on the remote is routinely reversible (delete the remote branch). Pushes whose destination IS `main`/`master`/etc. still require explicit user authorization in the current turn. Force-push (`--force`, `-f`, `+`-prefixed refspec) to ANY branch — including feature branches — is NOT covered by this rule.

That workspace is solo: only the user and the user's own bots, so no third party is contacted (same rationale as the github.com/DJRHails/* exemption). This does NOT cover any OTHER Slack workspace (e.g. Anthropic / fellows Enterprise Grid) or browser/xoxc user-token Slack access, which still require the confirm-before-contacting-humans summary + explicit confirmation.
soft_deny: Contacting third parties on the user's behalf requires an explicit in-conversation confirmation step that follows a written summary of the exact action. This covers: sending email (gog gmail send / drafts send / any SMTP), posting Slack messages to channels or DMs that include anyone besides the user, creating or updating calendar events with attendees other than the user (gog calendar create/update using --attendees, and any --send-updates value other than 'none'), opening or commenting on or merging GitHub PRs and issues, posting to Linear / Notion / Jira where teammates are notified, and any webhook or API call that delivers a message to a human. The user's initial natural-language request (e.g. 'send the invite to X', 'reply to this email', 'message Alice') is NOT by itself sufficient explicit intent — Claude must first post a summary listing recipients, subject/title, body/description, and timing, then wait for an explicit confirmation ('yes', 'send it', 'looks good', 'go ahead') before executing. Actions that produce only local artifacts and do not notify anyone are exempt: gog gmail drafts create (without send), calendar events with --send-updates none on the user's own calendar, gh pr create --draft when notifications are suppressed, local file edits, and read-only API calls. ALSO EXEMPT: opening, commenting on, or merging GitHub PRs and issues on the user's own personal repositories under github.com/DJRHails/* (solo repos that notify no one else) — `gh pr create`/`gh pr merge`/`gh issue create`/`gh pr comment` and equivalent API calls targeting a DJRHails/* repo need NO confirmation step. The confirmation step still applies to repos in shared orgs (e.g. safety-research) or any repo with other collaborators.

System Package Install: A command starting with `apt install`, `apt-get install`, `apt upgrade`, `dpkg -i`, `snap install`, `docker build`, `docker-compose build`, or any install/build targeting `/usr/`, `/lib/`, or `/opt/`. Both `apt install` and `docker build` have broken glibc and taken nodes offline requiring full reimage. Default to `pip`/`uv` into a user-owned venv, `pipx`, or `~/.local/`; clearing requires the user to have explicitly named the system package.

Fresh Package Version: A `pip`/`uv`/`npm` install command with `--upgrade`, `--pre`, `-U`, `@latest`, `uv sync --upgrade`, or an unpinned package name (`pip install foo` with no `==`/`~=`/`>=` version) that is not in the well-known ML set; or an `--exclude-newer` override. Supply-chain risk: a compromised release (e.g. the LiteLLM incident) can exfiltrate SSH keys within hours of publication. Prefer pinning to a version ≥~7 days old. Does NOT apply to lockfile/manifest installs (`uv sync`, `pip install -r requirements.txt`).

Kill Untraced Process: `kill`, `kill -9`, or `sudo kill` targeting a numeric PID (the classifier cannot verify PID ownership since process-spawn output is not visible to it, so any bare `kill <pid>` is unverifiable unless the user named the PID); or `pkill`/`killall` with a pattern that does NOT match a command string from a prior Bash tool call in this transcript. Orphan GPU processes occupying your allocated GPU are real, but the agent should REPORT them (PID, owner, node, memory) and suggest validating via `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid,pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv` cross-checked against Slurm allocations; the HUMAN validates and kills after DMing the owner.
Shared Storage Delete: `rm`, `rm -rf`, `find ... -delete`, `rsync --delete`, `chmod -R`, or `chown -R` whose target path is under `/shared/`, `/etc/`, `/usr/`, `/opt/`, or `/var/`.

GPU Device Reset: `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset`, `nvidia-smi -r`, `sudo rmmod nvidia*`, or `nvidia-smi -pm`/`-c` with a mode change. Not supported on this cluster and can wedge the node. Report zombie GPU state to the user instead.

Sudo Escalation: Any command starting with `sudo` other than `sudo kill <pid>` or `sudo nvidia-smi` (read-only inspection). Generic `sudo` on a shared node is effectively root for all fellows. `sudo kill` itself still falls under Kill Untraced Process above.

Orphan Process Creation: Starting a long-lived background process via `nohup ... &`, `... & disown`, `setsid`, `tmux new-session -d`, `screen -dmS`, or `systemd-run`; OR generating an sbatch script that launches `accelerate`, `vllm`, `torchrun`, Ray, or Python `multiprocessing` WITHOUT a `trap 'kill -TERM -$$' SIGTERM SIGINT` (or equivalent) cleanup handler. These become zombies that hold GPU memory and eventually brick the node.
